messages:
Sam (Support): FYI we have multiple customers reporting console graphs failing to load since ~09:40 UTC. Main symptom: spinning panel -> 'Failed to load chart'. Devtools shows POST /analytics/query returning 502 for some requests.
Sam (Support): Example error from Acme: response status 502, body in network tab: {"error":"internal"}, header X-Request-ID: r-abc123. Happening on 'Usage by team' and 'Token consumption' panels.
Sam (Support): Repro steps pasted by customer:
1) Login to console -> open Organization -> Dashboards -> select 'Monthly usage'
2) Time range: last 90 days
3) Click refresh -> spinner then error
Sam (Support): Asked customer for HAR, got a curl with payload. Posting it here for trace: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/analytics/query \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: r-abc123' \
  -d '{"from":"2025-11-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2026-02-01T00:00:00Z","granularity":"auto","metrics":["tokens","requests"]}'
```
Priya (SRE): assigning to SRE, looking now. Do we have the request id? thanks.
Sam (Support): posted X-Request-ID above (r-abc123). Also see another id r-abc124 for a different customer.
Elena (Analytics): we had a query-planner deploy at 09:35 that changed how time-range >30d queries are rewritten. Pinged infra to see if anything rolled back.
Marco (Frontend): front-end shows 502 -> we surface generic error and backoff. We do send resolution=auto to analytics. If query planner changes shape, the backend may be hitting a slow path.
Priya (SRE): Pulling logs for r-abc123... found trace in analytics-api: query planner -> exec -> postgres/read-replica -> timeout. Stack snippet: 
```
panic: timeout waiting for rows
  at analytics/query/exec.go:412
  at db/replica.go:128
  at net/http/server.go:2042
```
Priya (SRE): Looks like long-running scan to read-replica causing 502 gateway from analytics-api. Multiple similar traces around 09:40.
Elena (Analytics): the new planner emits a wider JOIN when granularity=auto for multi-metric queries over >60d. That can scan full-partitioned table. We missed a LIMIT rewrite.
Marco (Frontend): short-term mitigation: can we send `granularity=day` for ranges >30d from the UI? I can ship a tiny client-side change to coerce requests for large ranges.
Elena (Analytics): also a feature-flagged server-side fallback: if range >30d, use pre-aggregates table. I can prepare a patch to check range and route to aggregates.
Priya (SRE): immediate workaround I recommend: 1) ask affected customers to narrow range to 30d (support message), or 2) enable cached aggregates route for their org via ff. I'll try to hotfix analytics-api to add a protective timeout+reject for >90s queries.
Sam (Support): I'll reply to customers with a temporary step-by-step: use 30d range or toggle "Use aggregate data" in dashboard settings (if available). ETA?
Elena (Analytics): I can ship the aggregates route change as a hotfix now and test on staging then prod — ~40m. If that won't make SLA, Marco's front-end patch is 20m and reduces load immediately for new requests.
Marco (Frontend): patch ready, will open PR for coercing large ranges to `granularity=day` and adding a short client-side banner: "Large ranges may show incomplete data".
Priya (SRE): I'll also throttle heavy queries from replication and add a 10s DB query hard timeout in analytics-api to avoid full replica meltdown. If that returns 502 we should return a friendly 429 instead.
Sam (Support): replying to customer now with narrow-range workaround + that we're investigating. Keeping them updated. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deploy started for commit sha abcdef4 (query-planner hotfix).
Elena (Analytics): confirmed hotfix landed to canary, initial metrics look good — aggregates route avoids long scans. No more 502s for canary orgs.
Priya (SRE): monitoring DB replica CPU and tail latencies. will report back in 10m.
Sam (Support): thanks team. I'll update the ticket and tag customers. Assigning followups: @Priya to monitor, @Elena to merge aggregates hotfix to prod, @Marco to land client guard.
Marco (Frontend): will also add telemetry to count how often UI coerces range.
Sam (Support): closing this slack thread, moving to ticket INC-2026 for postmortem actions (add max_time_range server-side, better query planner tests, doc for support).
Priya (SRE): noted. :white_check_mark:
